newsitem.title: FRANCE: Royal Brunei plans Paris GSA ahead of November service.
newsitem.headline: Royal Brunei plans Paris GSA ahead of November service.

text.p: Royal Brunei Airlines, said it was looking to appoint a Paris-based cargo sales agent in preparation for the launch a twice-weekly Boeing 767-300 passenger service between Charles de Gaulle and Brunei Darussalam later this year.
Royal Brunei already operates a daily 767-300 passenger service from London and a three times weekly service from Frankfurt to Brunei.

"Subject to French government approval, the Paris-Brunei service is scheduled to begin in November 1997, operating to a twice-weekly frequency," said Royal Brunei Area manager, Europe, Sandra McGough.
She added: "We have already drawn up a short-list of Paris-based gsas and there's a chance we'll make our choice in the next month."
Royal Brunei's gsas at London and Frankfurt are respectively Ohio Express and ATC.

"Given that Brunei is heavily-dependent on exports, we see a good deal of scope in developing ex-Paris airfreight -- to Brunei and onward destinations -- with the 767-300 capable of handlingup to 18 tonnes per flight. -Reuter News Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44-171-542-7706 Fax-017
